region.lalibela.intro: The mountains of Lasta, where the Zagwe kings had churches carved straight down into red rock. People plough steep slopes, fast more than two hundred days a year, and believe angels helped the stonecutters at night.
region.aksum.intro: An ancient holy city in the north: stone stelae, the old church of Mary of Zion and the tradition of the Ark of the Covenant, brought by a son of Solomon. Pilgrims come here, and kings are crowned here.
region.shewa.intro: A fertile plateau at the heart of the Solomonic kingdom. There is no fixed capital: the king moves with a huge camp of tents, and every village on his road must feed the court and the army.
region.harar.intro: A walled Muslim city in the east and the chief city of the Adal sultanate. Narrow lanes, mosques, markets selling coffee, cloth and salt, and caravans setting out for the sea at Zeila.
